sections.title: Document type and word splitter
sections.what: Describes the search as word matching done offline, with a filter for the cutoff applied first. Defines a document with an observed time, and a splitter that turns text into lowercase words.
sections.why: Stated in the header: deterministic, offline, temporal filter first.
sections.watch_out: Numbers are treated as words, so a query containing a year matches any document that mentions that year.

sections.name: retrieve
sections.title: Find the best matching documents
sections.what: Finds the documents that best match a query. It drops documents after the cutoff and from disallowed sources, scores the rest by matching words weighted by rarity, breaks ties by newest first, and returns up to five.
sections.why: Likely reason: brief generation needs a few relevant, permitted, pre-cutoff sources.
sections.watch_out: An invalid cutoff raises an error, but an empty query quietly returns nothing, which can look like missing data.

summary: Searches stored documents for the words in a query and returns the most relevant ones observed before the cutoff.
purpose: Give the generator relevant context without future or disallowed material.
why: The header says it is deterministic and offline, and the cutoff filter runs first so a brief cannot know the future.
how: 1) Check the cutoff date is valid. 2) Keep documents observed by the cutoff and allowed by the source check. 3) Split the query and each document into words. 4) Score each document, giving rarer words more weight. 5) Drop zero scores, sort by score then newest, and keep the top few.
inputs: Query text, a list of documents with observed times, the cutoff date, a function that says whether a source is allowed, and an optional result count.
outputs: Up to five matching documents, each with its id, source id, text and observed time.
risks: Word matching misses synonyms, and numbers match loosely. Results depend entirely on what the source check allows through.
debug: If nothing comes back, check the query words appear in the documents and that observed times are before the cutoff. If a poor match ranks high, check the query length and rarer-word weighting. If it throws, check the cutoff date format.
